writeup: TIC 405529940 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 1.0266 days. TESS photometry reveals a primary eclipse causing a 3.00% dimming of the star's light, detected with a signal-to-noise ratio of 85.4. A secondary eclipse was not detected. Pixel-level image analysis confirms the signal at the target location, with a difference-imaging peak signal-to-noise of 31.2, though the centroid shows a 2.8 arcsecond offset from the cataloged position. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel find. The machine-learning screening score of 0.42 indicates moderate confidence in the result. No data quality issues were identified in the automated analysis pipeline.
